doc: LEADERBOARD_PRD.md §5.1 — the single source of truth for metrics. The build reads this file; nothing about a metric is hard-coded in the front end. Metric names are EVAL.md names; a metric's identity is the (arm, key) pair, because `crps` exists on both arms and the two are different instruments.

candi_self_comparison_bar.source: AGENTS.md §7.2 — a seed change alone moves pooled imputation CRPS by 0.1195 on the full EIC panel
candi_self_comparison_bar.note: CANDI version-over-version delta arrows only. This is NOT a cross-method noise floor; the cross-method floor for count-arm macro CRPS is the metric's own `floor` field.

pointwise.label: Point-wise
pointwise.note: The point tier — scoreable for any method.
pointwise.eli5: How close is the predicted track to the truth, bin by bin, and does it rank the tallest bins correctly? Every method can be scored here. These numbers are in p-value space.

distributional.label: Distributional
distributional.note: Pval-arm Gaussian CRPS with its calibration companions. PI ruling 2026-08-26: pval CRPS always renders with pit_ks and coverage_95.
distributional.eli5: Does the method's full predicted distribution match the truth, not just its centre? Fine to rank on; the absolute CRPS is not a calibrated number yet. Always shown with PIT KS and 95% coverage.

peaks.label: Peaks
peaks.note: Enters the composite only if every ranked row has it (PRD §5.1) — the §5.2 completeness rule the build applies to every composite category.
peaks.eli5: Are the positions the method treats as peaks actually the peaks in the truth? Only comparable when a method emits a peak score. Always quoted with the peak base rate.

count_arm.label: Count space
count_arm.note: PRD §5.2 — pval-only rivals have no count arm and no counts are invented (B1b). Sub-board ranks only the methods that emit counts; the composite does not move when it grows a row.
count_arm.eli5: The same distributional scoring, but on raw read counts rather than p-values. Only methods that emit counts appear. Count and p-value numbers never share a column or a chart axis. CRPS always shows its oracle-scaled / scale-error split, with the ~0.09 noise floor.

loss.label: Loss
loss.note: PRD §5.2 — loss-tier NLLs never enter the composite: different distribution families make them incomparable across methods; they show per-family only.
loss.eli5: The training loss on data the method did not train on. Different methods use different loss families, so these numbers cannot be ranked against each other. Count-space NLL and p-value-space NLL stay in separate columns.

covariate_diagnostics.label: Covariate sensitivity
covariate_diagnostics.note: PRD §5.3 — rivals have no covariate-conditioned decoder, so these rank CANDI versions against each other, never methods.
covariate_diagnostics.eli5: Does CANDI actually use the experimental settings we tell it (depth, assay, read length, run type)? Rivals have no such decoder, so this ranks CANDI versions against each other only. The box is empty until a CANDI checkpoint is scored by the internal bench — the path that can change a prompt and re-decode.
covariate_diagnostics.absent_note: No current row has these numbers. They ask whether CANDI's decoder uses the experimental settings we tell it (depth, assay, read length, run type): the scorer changes one setting and watches the prediction move. That needs the model. Every stamped row was scored from saved prediction tracks by python -m candi.bench.external, or by the 2019 placement scorer — neither path sees a covariate-conditioned decoder, so neither can emit covuse, covshare, depthdir, depthcounterfact, covspec, depthblind, or biokeep. Rivals have no such decoder in any case.
covariate_diagnostics.will_populate: These cells will fill in for CANDI-lineage rows scored by the internal python -m candi.bench C-block (default --blocks includes C). They cannot come from candi.bench.external.

metrics.floor_note: t57 measured this column's floors (results/t57/FLOOR_MEMO.md, floors.json) and found NO single number: the target-clustered floor is per-method (bootstrap SD roughly a tenth of the method's own macro; avg 0.031, eDICE 0.079, marginal 0.277), and a between-method gap is significant only when it clears its PAIRED 95% CI (floor_calc.py, 10,000 replicates, seed 0). ChromImpute-vs-eDICE (+0.0141) sits inside its paired floor; both rivals' gap to the avg baseline (~+0.27, ~5 paired SDs) is real. Until per-pair floors are wired into the tie machinery this column ranks plain and its deltas are not greyed.
metrics.calibration_note: Point-only rivals get a constant per-assay spread (the B1a device). It is known-miscalibrated: PIT KS ≈ 0.37 and 95% coverage ≈ 0.98, the same across those rivals. Rank on this column; do not read the absolute CRPS as calibrated.
metrics.eli5: A score for the whole predicted distribution in p-value space. Fine to rank methods on; not a calibrated absolute. Always shown with PIT KS and 95% coverage.
metrics.label: CRPS (Gaussian, p-value)
Coverage 95
metrics.note: Nominal 0.95; a companion, never ranked — distance from nominal is not a direction.

metrics.label: AUPRC
metrics.note: EVAL.md — always quoted with peak_base_rate; an auprc from a count-only checkpoint is a coverage ranking, not a peak metric.

metrics.label: Gaussian NLL
metrics.note: Quoted with its signal_target_transform or not at all (EVAL.md); shown per distribution family only.

metrics.floor_note: Target-clustered bootstrap noise floor on macro CRPS, ~0.09 (AGENTS.md §7.2, frozen pre-CANDII panel). A seed change alone moves pooled CRPS by 0.1195 on the full EIC panel — that bar is for CANDI version-over-version arrows, not a cross-method floor.
metrics.eli5: A score for the whole predicted distribution over raw read counts. Always shown as a split: capability (oracle-scaled) plus a fixable scale error. The ~0.09 figure beside it is the noise floor — a gap smaller than that does not decide a rank.
metrics.label: CRPS (NB, counts)
NB NLL
metrics.note: Shown per distribution family only; never ranked cross-method.

metrics.label: depthcounterfact
metrics.note: Quotes with its 0.25 deterministic floor and no ceiling (EVAL.md).
